card.summary: H.R. 9368, the Voter ID Act, amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to set specific photo identification requirements for individuals voting in federal elections, both in person and by other methods. It defines acceptable photo identification, outlines provisional ballot rules for those lacking ID, requires states to provide free access to digital imaging devices for copying IDs, notifies voter registration applicants of the ID rules, and establishes a federal grant program to help states and tribal governments provide free photo IDs to individuals who cannot afford them.

card.summary: The Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act (or the SAVE America Act) requires individuals to provide documentary proof of U.S. citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections. It also requires voters to present valid photo identification when casting ballots in federal elections, either in person or alongside mail-in ballots. States must check their voter rolls against federal databases to remove noncitizens and establish processes for alternative proof or handling name discrepancies.

summary: S. 5271 amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to establish federal photo identification requirements for individuals voting in federal elections, covering both in-person and mail-in or absentee voting methods. It defines acceptable forms of identification, provides for provisional ballots under certain conditions, requires states to offer free public access to digital imaging devices for copying identification, and sets an effective date one day after enactment.

affected_groups.effect: Must provide a valid physical photo ID for in-person voting or a copy of an ID (or Social Security number and affidavit) for non-in-person voting, or use provisional ballots with strict follow-up rules.
Must enforce photo ID rules for federal elections, handle provisional ballots under new timeline requirements, and notify voters during registration.
Exempted from the requirement to submit an ID copy or Social Security number with non-in-person ballots.
affected_groups.group: Absent uniformed services voters and certain disabled or elderly voters

affected_groups.effect: Must ensure public access to free digital imaging devices in buildings such as courts, libraries, and police stations for copying photo IDs.

key_provisions: Prohibits state or local election officials from giving a federal election ballot to an in-person voter who does not present a valid physical photo ID.
Permits individuals without a photo ID to cast a provisional ballot, which will only count if the voter presents a valid photo ID or a religious-objection affidavit within three days.
Requires voters using voting methods other than in-person voting to submit either a copy of a valid photo ID or the last four digits of their Social Security number along with an affidavit.
Exempts absent uniformed services voters and certain elderly or disabled individuals from the photo ID requirements for non-in-person voting.
Requires states to provide free public access to digital imaging devices in government buildings for individuals to copy their photo IDs.
Defines valid photo IDs as certain driver's licenses, state-issued ID cards, U.S. passports, military IDs, and Tribal government-issued IDs.
Requires states to notify individuals of these photo identification requirements when they apply to register to vote, including online registrations.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budgetary allocations for states to provide free digital imaging devices.
Detailed enforcement mechanisms or penalties for states that fail to comply with the new requirements.
summary_detail.plain_summary: S. 5271 amends the Help America Vote Act of 2002 to establish federal photo identification requirements for individuals voting in federal elections, covering both in-person and mail-in or absentee voting methods. It defines acceptable forms of identification, provides for provisional ballots under certain conditions, requires states to offer free public access to digital imaging devices for copying identification, and sets an effective date one day after enactment.
summary_detail.significance: This bill introduces nationwide photo identification requirements and specific verification procedures for all federal elections, impacting how voters cast ballots and how states administer voting processes.
